tuner_timing.justification: This configuration explores higher scheduler latencies and granularity to potentially improve throughput by reducing context switching overhead, while also preventing deep C-states and enabling NAPI busy-polling for lower network latency.

Increased scheduling granularity, latency, and migration cost to potentially reduce context switching and improve cache locality, while also raising napi_busy_poll for better network throughput. This explores a more aggressive configuration based on the previous promising results.

Increased CFS scheduler latency (latency_ns) slightly, as the previous increase from 60M to 70M yielded improved throughput. This step aims to further explore the higher end of the latency range to maximize performance.

The previous iteration showed a slight decrease in throughput when latency_ns was increased from 70M to 80M. This iteration will explore a slightly lower latency_ns value to confirm the optimal region around 70M and refine the search.

Based on the recent trials, throughput peaked around 70M latency_ns and declined slightly at 65M and 80M. This iteration refines the search for optimal latency_ns by exploring a value slightly above the previous peak, while maintaining other parameters that have shown good performance.

The highest throughput was achieved with a relatively high latency_ns. I am exploring a slightly higher value for latency_ns to see if throughput continues to improve, while keeping other parameters stable as they have consistently yielded good results.
Given the best performance at 72,000,000 ns and a slight drop at 80,000,000 ns, we are exploring a value between these two points to refine the optimal latency_ns and account for measurement noise.

Given the noisy data, I am refining the latency_ns around the previous best value of 72,000,000 ns to confirm the local optimum. Other parameters remain stable as they contributed to the highest throughput.

Re-testing the configuration that yielded the highest throughput (11.00) will help confirm if that peak was robust or due to noise, given the variability in recent trials. This is an exploitation step to refine around the most promising region.
Given the noisy data and the peak around 72M for latency_ns, we are exploring a slightly lower value to confirm the optimal range and ensure the robustness of the tuning.

The highest throughput was consistently observed around latency_ns=72,000,000. By keeping this value and slightly increasing napi_busy_poll, I aim to explore if further network processing efficiency can improve overall throughput, given the noisy measurements.

Re-testing the configuration that previously yielded the highest throughput (11.00) to confirm its robustness and optimal performance, especially after a recent dip in throughput when napi_busy_poll was increased. This helps to validate the optimal region amidst noisy measurements.

The previous best configurations consistently used similar parameters. We are slightly increasing migration_cost_ns to investigate if further discouraging task migration improves cache locality and throughput, while maintaining optimal latency and NAPI busy poll settings.

Reverting migration_cost_ns to its previously optimal value of 8,000,000 ns, which was part of the highest throughput configurations. Making a small adjustment to latency_ns to further explore the immediate vicinity of the previous peak.

The previous best configuration yielded high throughput. I will slightly increase min_granularity_ns and wakeup_granularity_ns to explore if reducing scheduler overhead can further improve throughput, while keeping other parameters at their previously optimal values.

The best throughput was achieved with migration_cost_ns=8,000,000. An adjacent value of 10,000,000 previously yielded a respectable 9.50 throughput, suggesting this region is promising. I will explore an intermediate value to refine the optimal setting for migration cost.
Refining around the best observed configuration (throughput 11.00) by slightly adjusting napi_busy_poll to explore the immediate vicinity and confirm robustness in a noisy environment.

Given the noisy performance data and recent throughput fluctuations, we are re-testing the previously best-performing configuration to confirm its stability and robustness against system variability. This helps validate if the high throughput was an outlier or a consistent result for these parameters.

Slightly adjusting napi_busy_poll to 450 to explore a value between the previous best (400) and a slightly higher value (500) that yielded decent results, aiming to refine the optimal point given the noisy environment.

Reverting to the configuration that previously yielded the highest throughput (11.00 and 10.40) to re-evaluate its performance and confirm robustness, especially after recent deviations resulted in lower throughput. This is an exploitation step to confirm the promising region.

Given the noisy performance data and extensive exploration around the optimal region, we are making a small, incremental adjustment to latency_ns and migration_cost_ns to refine the current best configuration. This step aims to confirm robustness and test for any marginal gains within the identified high-throughput zone.

Reverting to the configuration that previously yielded the highest throughput (11.00) will help confirm its stability and performance in the presence of noise, ensuring we are not chasing noisy peaks. This step aims to re-validate the most promising region found so far.
Conducting a micro-adjustment to scheduler latency and migration cost to explore the immediate vicinity of the current peak, aiming for finer optimization in a noisy environment.

Given the extensive local exploration around the best-performing configuration (11.00 throughput) and the noisy data, this iteration aims to slightly increase min_granularity_ns and wakeup_granularity_ns to potentially reduce context switching overhead. This explores a slightly less aggressive scheduling policy without deviating too far from the promising region, as previous larger increases to 20M were detrimental.

Reverting to the previously identified best configuration (from Iter 7 and 11) to re-evaluate its performance and confirm stability, especially after a noisy low result in the last iteration. This helps to validate the optimal region and account for system variability.

Given the noisy metrics and consistent high performance around the current best configuration, I am making a very slight perturbation to latency_ns and migration_cost_ns to probe the immediate vicinity of the peak. This aims to confirm robustness and potentially find a slightly better optimum within the noisy environment.
Given the high noise, we are re-testing the configuration that previously yielded the highest throughput (11.00) to confirm its robustness and identify the true performance ceiling.

Reverting to the configuration that previously yielded the highest throughput values (11.00 and 10.40 multiple times) is a robust strategy given the high measurement noise and lack of consistent improvement from recent minor perturbations. This configuration appears to be in the optimal region for maximizing throughput.

Given the noisy measurements and multiple high throughput results with the current configuration, we are in an exploitation phase. Re-evaluating the configuration that previously yielded the highest throughput (11.00) to confirm its robustness against noise and stability, as recent minor variations have shown decreased performance.

Given the noisy data and the stability of the best-performing region, I am slightly increasing min_granularity_ns and wakeup_granularity_ns to explore if a minor adjustment around the optimal 15M value can yield further improvements, inspired by iter 28's decent result with 16M. This tests robustness within the identified optimal region.

Reverting latency_ns to 72,000,000 to re-exploit the configuration that previously yielded the highest throughput, as the current value of 80,000,000 resulted in lower performance. This is a direct exploitation step to confirm robustness in the promising region.

Reverting to the historically best performing configuration to re-evaluate its robustness and confirm the peak throughput, given the high noise in recent measurements and lack of consistent improvement from minor adjustments. This step aims to stabilize around the optimal region.

In the exploitation phase, we are making small adjustments to parameters around the best-performing configuration to refine the optimal balance. Slightly increasing NAPI busy poll and decreasing migration cost explores a more aggressive polling strategy with reduced migration overhead.
Reverting napi_busy_poll to 400, which was part of the best-performing configuration (11.25 throughput), to re-evaluate its robustness and confirm the impact of recent minor changes.

Given the noisy measurements, re-evaluating the configuration that previously yielded the highest throughput (11.25) helps confirm its robustness and ensures we are consistently operating within the identified optimal region.
